The 1986 World Exposition on Transportation and Communication, or simply Expo 86, was a world's fair held in Vancouver
is named after Lord Stanley of Preston, the governor general of Canada, who donated it as an award to Canada's top-ranking amateur ice hockey club
items.note: Correct (Stanley Park is named after the same Lord Stanley, per en:Stanley_Park), but the question gives the answer away: "Stanley" plus "famous trophy" is Stanley Cup for anyone in a Canadian room. Suggested rewording that keeps the fact but needs knowledge: "The Governor General who gave Stanley Park its name also donated a trophy first awarded in 1893. In which sport?" (answer: ice hockey).

items.quote: Gastown was Vancouver's first neighbourhood and was named for "Gassy" Jack Deighton
The Vancouver Canucks are a professional ice hockey team based in Vancouver
The Lions compete in the West Division of the Canadian Football League (CFL), and play their home games at BC Place
The Lions Gate Bridge, opened in 1938 and officially known as the First Narrows Bridge, is a suspension bridge that crosses the first narrows of Burrard Inlet
items.note: Accept "First Narrows Bridge", its official name. The Ironworkers Memorial (Second Narrows) Bridge also crosses Burrard Inlet but not from Stanley Park, and is not a suspension bridge.

items.quote: The city takes its name from George Vancouver, who explored the inner harbour of Burrard Inlet in 1792
In 1969, Greenpeace was founded in Vancouver
items.note: Answer is solid, but the date in the question is not: en:Vancouver says 1969 (the Don't Make a Wave Committee), en:Greenpeace says 1971. The answer does not change, but consider dropping "in the early 1970s" so no one challenges the premise.

items.quote: The Strait of Georgia or the Georgia Strait is an arm of the Salish Sea between Vancouver Island and the extreme southwestern mainland coast of British Columbia
items.note: Accept "Georgia Strait". "Salish Sea" is the wider body and is not a strait, so the question's "strait" excludes it.
